rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both directives address conferral or acquisition of competitive civil-service status for State Department or Foreign Service personnel whose transfer prevented them from obtaining that status in a former position. Most distinctively, both use the same counterfactual predicate: the employee could have acquired competitive status if the employee had remained in the former position. The child adapts C15's class-based administrative machinery into individualized relief for Miss Donnellon. C06 and C11 concern civil-service status or Commission authority but lack this distinctive factual and operative correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Civil Service Commission is hereby authorized to confer a competitive status upon Miss Winifred R. Donnellon
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall be considered as having a competitive status
shared_material.explanation: Both use presidential action to secure competitive status for personnel whose government service circumstances obstructed the ordinary route.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If Miss Donnellon had remained in the position in the Department of State from which she was transferred in 1945 at the convenience of the Department, she would have become eligible in 1946 to acquire a competitive status under noncompetitive procedures of the Civil Service Commission.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: who could, with the approval of the head of the agency in which he was serving, have been given a competitive status under Civil Service Rule III if he had remained in his former position
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive shared counterfactual formulation tying eligibility for competitive status to remaining in a former position rather than being transferred or assigned elsewhere.

shared_material.child_excerpt: pursuant to the recommendation of the Secretary of State
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Civil Service Commission is authorized, after consultation with the Department of State, to prescribe such rules and regulations as may be necessary
shared_material.explanation: Both coordinate the Civil Service Commission and Department of State in providing competitive-status relief, though the child converts the general framework into a named-person authorization.
